Test the association of a mosaic with and without clustering

Source: R/mosaic_test.R
mosaic_test.Rd

mosaic_test() runs the tests behind mosaic_plot() and mosaic_analysis() and returns their results as a data frame. Give it the same object you would draw: a network, a netobject_group, a three-way table, or a data frame with two variables. By default it runs Pearson's chi-square, which treats every count as independent, next to the five tests that allow for counts nested in actors (sequences, students, teams), so the table shows what the nesting changes.

The tests are those of Nested data in mosaic_analysis(): "rao_scott" (Rao-Scott corrected F), "donner_klar" (Pearson divided by the cluster-size inflation factor), "cmh" (generalised Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel with each actor as a stratum), "gee" (Wald test of a marginal model with cluster-robust covariance) and "glmm" (Wald test of a log-linear mixed model, needs lme4). "chisq" is Pearson's test on the pooled table. As in the mosaics, a network's source state and a group are the predictors.

Not every test fits every design: Donner-Klar needs one variable that is constant within actors (the group of a netobject_group), and CMH needs both to vary within actors (the states of a network). When several methods are asked for, a test that cannot run on the design gives a row of NA with the reason in note; asked for alone, it raises the error.

Usage

mosaic_test(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
mosaic_test(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
mosaic_test(
  x,
  method = c("chisq", "rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee", "glmm"),
  actor = NULL,
  level = c("test", "cells"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'htna'
mosaic_test(
  x,
  method = c("chisq", "rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee", "glmm"),
  actor = NULL,
  level = c("test", "cells"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
mosaic_test(
  x,
  method = c("chisq", "rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee", "glmm"),
  actor = NULL,
  level = c("test", "cells"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'array'
mosaic_test(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'table'
mosaic_test(
  x,
  method = c("chisq", "rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee", "glmm"),
  level = c("test", "cells"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
mosaic_test(
  x,
  var1,
  var2,
  actor,
  method = c("chisq", "rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee", "glmm"),
  level = c("test", "cells"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A netobject or htna network (relative or frequency, with its sequences), a netobject_group, a three-way table or array (rows x columns x actors), or a data frame (with var1, var2 and actor). A co-occurrence network raises an error of class nestimate_mosaic_undirected: it counts each pair of states in both mirrored cells and the pairs of a sequence share its positions, so its counts are not independent and the tests would not hold their level (under independence Pearson's test rejected 200 of 200 simulated tables at 0.05). mosaic_plot() still draws it. A tna model or a group_tna (package tna) is first rebuilt as a network from its own sequences (see as_netobject()). actor is read from the metadata the model keeps (attr(model$data, "meta"), kept when the model is built from tna::prepare_data()); a model without it raises nestimate_actor_missing.

...

Not used; a name given here raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

method

The tests to run, any of "chisq", "rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee" and "glmm". Default: all six.

actor

The actor column(s), as in permutation(): for a network or netobject_group, NULL (default) makes every sequence its own actor, and the name of a metadata column (such as a team) pools the sequences that share its value; for a data frame, the column(s) that identify the actors (required). Several names give nested levels, outermost first: "glmm" models each level, the other tests use the outermost. Not used for a three-way table, whose third dimension is the actor.

level

"test" (default) for one row per test, "cells" for one row per cell per test with the cell's residual.

var1, var2

For a data frame: the names of the two variables; var1 is the predictor.

Value

A data frame. With level = "test", one row per test: method, test (its name), statistic (F for Rao-Scott, chi-square otherwise), df, df2 (the Rao-Scott denominator degrees of freedom), p_value, n (counts in the table), clusters (actors the test used), design_effect (Rao-Scott's mean generalised design effect, or Donner-Klar's mean inflation factor), icc (Donner-Klar's intracluster correlation) and note (why a test did not run, the caution on the GEE Wald test, else NA). With level = "cells", one row per cell and test: method, the two variables (from/to for a network, group/state for a group, the variable names for a data frame, row/column for a table), observed and residual (the residual the mosaic draws for that method; NA where undefined). An unsupported input raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

References

Rao, J. N. K., & Scott, A. J. (1984). On chi-squared tests for multiway contingency tables with cell proportions estimated from survey data. The Annals of Statistics, 12(1), 46–60. doi:10.1214/aos/1176346391

Donner, A., & Klar, N. (1994). Methods for comparing event rates in intervention studies when the unit of allocation is a cluster. American Journal of Epidemiology, 140(3), 279–289. doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a117247

Landis, J. R., Heyman, E. R., & Koch, G. G. (1978). Average partial association in three-way contingency tables: A review and discussion of alternative tests. International Statistical Review, 46(3), 237–254. doi:10.2307/1402373

Liang, K.-Y., & Zeger, S. L. (1986). Longitudinal data analysis using generalized linear models. Biometrika, 73(1), 13–22. doi:10.1093/biomet/73.1.13

See also

mosaic_plot(), mosaic_analysis()

Examples

data(group_regulation_long, package = "Nestimate")
net <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "frequency",
                     format = "long", actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
                     order = "Time")
mosaic_test(net, method = c("chisq", "rao_scott"), actor = "Group")
#>      method      test  statistic       df      df2 p_value     n clusters
#> 1     chisq   Pearson 15435.2605 64.00000       NA       0 25533       NA
#> 2 rao_scott Rao-Scott   227.7646 39.41762 7844.106       0 25533      200
#>   design_effect icc note
#> 1            NA  NA <NA>
#> 2      1.058882  NA <NA>
# \donttest{
# Several tests, sequences nested in teams (the default runs them all,
# the mixed model included)
mosaic_test(net, method = c("rao_scott", "donner_klar", "cmh", "gee"),
            actor = "Group")
#>        method                    test  statistic       df      df2 p_value
#> 1   rao_scott               Rao-Scott   227.7646 39.41762 7844.106       0
#> 2 donner_klar             Donner-Klar         NA       NA       NA      NA
#> 3         cmh Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel 15167.3307 64.00000       NA       0
#> 4         gee                GEE Wald         NA       NA       NA      NA
#>       n clusters design_effect icc
#> 1 25533      200      1.058882  NA
#> 2 25533       NA            NA  NA
#> 3 25533      200            NA  NA
#> 4 25533       NA            NA  NA
#>                                                                                          note
#> 1                                                                                        <NA>
#> 2                        Donner-Klar needs one variable that is constant within every cluster
#> 3                                                                                        <NA>
#> 4 GEE: the cluster-robust covariance has rank 63, below the 64 degrees of freedom of the test

# Cell residuals of one test
head(mosaic_test(net, method = "rao_scott", actor = "Group",
                 level = "cells"))
#>      method  from         to observed   residual
#> 1 rao_scott adapt      adapt        0 -1.9966253
#> 2 rao_scott adapt   cohesion      139 17.4827797
#> 3 rao_scott adapt  consensus      243 11.5347947
#> 4 rao_scott adapt coregulate       11 -4.6447682
#> 5 rao_scott adapt    discuss       30 -6.2361428
#> 6 rao_scott adapt    emotion       61  0.8545643
# }
